runbook:
## Inputs needed

- `<PALWORLD_IP>` — the IP address the palworld-server VM (106) will receive from DHCP on vmbr0. The engine can read this off the host once the VM is up.
- `<PALWORLD_USER>` — the non-root user account inside the VM that will run the server. Suggested default: `palworld` (rename if you like).

## Prerequisites

- VM 106 exists and is configured per T22 (confirmed in upstream output).
- The VM has a working network connection on vmbr0.
- The VM has an OS installed and reachable over SSH. If the VM has no OS yet, install one first (Ubuntu Server 22.04 LTS recommended for SteamCMD compatibility).

## Risk

- None of these steps are destructive to the host. All work happens inside VM 106.
- The SteamCMD install downloads several hundred MB from Valve's servers; ensure the VM has internet access.

## Run this

1. Install SteamCMD dependencies and create the service user:

```bash
ssh -o BatchMode=yes <PALWORLD_USER>@<PALWORLD_IP> "sudo -S -p '' bash -c 'dpkg --add-architecture i386 && apt-get update && apt-get install -y lib32gcc-s1 lib32stdc++6 curl wget file tar bzip2 gzip unzip python3'"
```

2. Create the SteamCMD directory and download SteamCMD:

```bash
ssh -o BatchMode=yes <PALWORLD_USER>@<PALWORLD_IP> "sudo -S -p '' bash -c 'mkdir -p /opt/steamcmd && cd /opt/steamcmd && curl -sqL \"https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/client/installer/steamcmd_linux.tar.gz\" | tar zxvf -'"
```

3. Run SteamCMD to install the PalWorld dedicated server:

```bash
ssh -o BatchMode=yes <PALWORLD_USER>@<PALWORLD_IP> "sudo -S -p '' bash -c '/opt/steamcmd/steamcmd.sh +force_install_dir /opt/palworld +login anonymous +app_update 2394010 validate +quit'"
```

4. Set ownership of the PalWorld directory to the service user:

```bash
ssh -o BatchMode=yes <PALWORLD_USER>@<PALWORLD_IP> "sudo -S -p '' bash -c 'chown -R <PALWORLD_USER>:<PALWORLD_USER> /opt/palworld'"
```

## Verify

- Confirm SteamCMD is installed and executable: `ssh -o BatchMode=yes <PALWORLD_USER>@<PALWORLD_IP> "ls -la /opt/steamcmd/steamcmd.sh"`
- Confirm the PalWorld server binary exists: `ssh -o BatchMode=yes <PALWORLD_USER>@<PALWORLD_IP> "ls -la /opt/palworld/PalServer.sh"`
- Confirm the server files are owned by the service user: `ssh -o BatchMode=yes <PALWORLD_USER>@<PALWORLD_IP> "ls -ld /opt/palworld"`

## Rollback

- If SteamCMD fails to download, check the VM's internet connectivity: `ssh -o BatchMode=yes <PALWORLD_USER>@<PALWORLD_IP> "ping -c 3 8.8.8.8"`
- If the PalWorld install fails, remove the partial install and retry: `ssh -o BatchMode=yes <PALWORLD_USER>@<PALWORLD_IP> "sudo -S -p '' bash -c 'rm -rf /opt/palworld && /opt/steamcmd/steamcmd.sh +force_install_dir /opt/palworld +login anonymous +app_update 2394010 validate +quit'"`
- If the VM is unreachable, verify it is running on the host: `qm status 106`
